cards.front: Class II cabinet airflow and clean-to-dirty layout
cards.back: The critical zone is ISO 5 (Class 100), with typical vertical HEPA airflow 0.45 m/s ±20%. Keep grilles and the front opening clear, do not overcrowd or stack, and arrange clean supplies → target culture → waste. A UV lamp does not replace chemical wiping, and a burner must not be used.

cards.front: Sterile-to-sterile manipulation rules
cards.back: Work with one cell line; use a fresh sterile pipette for each vessel or sample; hold closures above the opening or upright, never face down; approach from the side; move slowly and gently; do not talk over exposed product; sanitize gloves before opening and after dirty material.

cards.front: Sterility-control incubation schedule
cards.back: Incubate for at least 14 total days within 20–35 °C. When two temperatures are used, hold at least 7 days at 20–25 °C first, then at least 7 days at 30–35 °C.

cards.front: Mycoplasma detection and the limit of antibiotics
cards.back: Mycoplasmas are about 0.15–0.3 µm, can pass 0.22 µm filters and can grow without turbidity; 0.1 µm filtration and routine dedicated testing are needed. Penicillin-streptomycin may mask visible growth but does not sterilize the culture.

cards.front: Improved-Neubauer large-square volume and the concentration formula
cards.back: 1 mm × 1 mm × 0.1 mm = 0.1 µL = 10⁻⁴ mL, so viable cells/mL = mean unstained count per large square × 10,000 × dilution factor. Check the depth marked on your own chamber.

cards.front: Boundary rule, corners and the order of decisions
cards.back: Include cells touching the top or left line; exclude any cell touching the bottom or right line, even at a corner. Decide the boundary first, then the stain; excluded cells enter neither tally.

cards.front: Poisson counting uncertainty and what it leaves out
cards.back: About 100/√N percent for N cells counted: 100 cells give 10%, 400 give 5%. It excludes mixing, dilution, loading and classification errors, which replicate agreement cannot reveal.

cards.front: What trypan-blue viability does and does not show
cards.back: The fraction of counted cells with intact membranes at the moment of counting, read in serum-free solution within minutes. Not growth, function, phenotype, sterility or overall health.

cards.front: Nutrients, pH, osmolality, bicarbonate/CO₂ and phenol red
cards.back: Basal medium supplies formulation-specific salts and nutrients. pH and osmolality are different QC quantities. Bicarbonate buffering requires its specified CO₂ environment; phenol red indicates pH shifts but is not the buffer and shows neither osmolality nor sterility. Serum-free is not automatically fully defined.

cards.front: Final-volume rule for concentrated supplements
cards.back: V_stock = C_target × V_final/C_stock; then V_basal = V_final − ΣV_supplements. For 500 mL at 10% serum plus 1× glutamine from 100×: 50 mL serum + 5 mL stock + 445 mL basal = 500 mL final.

cards.front: Supplement handling and the filtration evidence boundary
cards.back: Reject expired/unidentified lots; preserve frozen/cold glutamine history and avoid repeated freeze–thaw. Heat-inactivate serum only for an application-specific reason. Use an aseptic 0.22 µm protein-compatible filter and an integrity test; neither clarity nor 0.22 µm filtration excludes mollicutes.

cards.front: Supplemented-medium QC, label, storage and release
cards.back: Record additions, component/filter lots, pH, osmolality and filter integrity. Incubate filtrate controls ≥7 days at 20–25 °C then ≥7 days at 30–35 °C and submit dedicated mycoplasma testing. Link dates/expiry and cell line; account for aliquots; store 2–8 °C dark and quarantine pending QC.

cards.front: Culture disposition before passaging
cards.back: Use growth state, morphology, medium and viability together. This simulation chooses 70–85% confluence for routine adherent passage and a separate 95% refusal/investigation branch. Suspension cultures use density and clumping rather than surface confluence. These are synthetic choices, not cell-line acceptance criteria.

cards.front: Adherent versus suspension passaging
cards.back: Adherent: inspect → remove medium → calcium/magnesium-free wash → dissociate → observe detachment → neutralize → collect/resuspend → count → seed. Suspension: mix/sample → count → dilute directly or transfer a portion and dilute; no substrate-detachment step.

cards.front: Target-density inoculum and fresh medium
cards.back: V_cells per flask = N_target/C_viable. V_fresh = V_final − V_cells. For n identical flasks multiply the per-flask inoculum by n. Example: 500000/(1.21 × 10⁶) = 0.413223 mL; at 12.0 mL final, fresh medium = 11.586777 mL.

cards.front: Split ratio, passage number and PDL
cards.back: A split ratio records a proportional transfer, not a guaranteed viable density. Passage number counts subculture events. PDL increment = log₂(Nf/N0); cumulative PDL = previous cumulative PDL + increment. Neither passage number nor PDL authenticates a cell line.

cards.front: Permeating versus non-permeating cryoprotectants
cards.back: DMSO and glycerol permeate membranes; trehalose, hydroxyethyl starch and poly(vinyl pyrrolidone) are non-permeating examples. Non-permeating agents remain extracellular and are not interchangeable with DMSO. Liquid nitrogen is a refrigerant. The simulation’s cold 4 °C dropwise DMSO rule and 10% final v/v are synthetic teaching choices.

cards.front: Two-factor injury, cooling and thawing
cards.back: Too slow: prolonged dehydration and concentrated-solute/solution stresses. Too fast: inadequate water loss and intracellular ice. Use a cell-appropriate intermediate history. Simulation: controlled rate or passive container at about 1 °C/min, −80 °C hold; then rapid 37 °C thaw, gradual dilution and DMSO removal. Exact tolerances are synthetic.

cards.front: Freeze/thaw volume and viability arithmetic
cards.back: Component volume = final volume × fraction. Vials = total viable cells/target per vial. Diluted fraction = initial fraction × initial volume/final volume. Residual DMSO % = remaining DMSO volume/final volume × 100. Conserved total cells: viable recovery = initial viable cells × post-thaw viability/pre-freeze viability.

cards.front: Storage, QC and bank-tier traceability
cards.back: This scenario uses LN₂ vapour, not liquid immersion, and records dewar/rack/box/position. Recount membrane integrity but do not infer growth, identity or sterility. Keep new stock quarantine_pending_qc and retain its master-seed/working-stock provenance for lesson 8; simulation completion is not release.

cards.front: Visible bacterial/fungal clues versus identification
cards.back: Turbidity and a pH shift are warning clues; small rods support a bacterial-pattern investigation and branching filaments/micro-colonies support a fungal-pattern investigation. Quarantine before identification; neither appearance nor a simplified stain/subculture names a species.

cards.front: Mycoplasma methods and their limits
cards.back: Culture is slow and can miss non-culturable strains; PCR needs target coverage and internal/positive/negative controls because carry-over and inhibitors mislead; DNA stain is non-specific and can be insensitive/subjective. Clear appearance, filtration, Gram stain and STR are not dedicated mycoplasma evidence.

cards.front: Disposition and antibiotic masking
cards.back: Quarantine first. Discard and replace routine visibly contaminated cultures; contain mycoplasma-positive cultures; hold an STR-mismatched line for identity investigation. Specialist rescue referral is exceptional. Antibiotics may mask growth without sterilising and are not a release pathway.

cards.front: STR reading and intake/source trace
cards.back: A locus contains short tandem repeats; allele calls across loci are compared with a traceable reference using a declared method. Match is not sterility/phenotype; mismatch triggers identity hold. Quarantine incoming lines, test locally, and join provenance, lot, equipment and handling records without copying donor data.

cards.front: Defined matrix: feeder-free is not substrate-free
cards.back: Use a compatible, traceable matrix with cold-liquid handling, complete even coverage and no drying. Record the actual lot. Recurrent differentiation after selective removal should trigger investigation rather than assumptions.

cards.front: Daily morphology, removal, feeding and density
cards.back: Score before disturbing, map and selectively remove differentiated areas, feed completely each day, and record residual/recurrent patterns. Synthetic routine: 42→60→78%; continue days 1–2 and passage day 3. Residual example: (18−15)/240 × 100 = 1.25%.

cards.front: Clump passage and allocation
cards.back: Use small clumps rather than default single cells, with gentle handling and a prepared matrix. 156 clumps/6 wells = 26 per well; clump counts do not predict viability or colony formation.

cards.front: Four QC questions plus an independent permission gate
cards.back: Mycoplasma = contamination; STR = identity; karyotype = large-scale genomic pattern; undifferentiated markers ≠ functional proof. Intake must clear quarantine and periodic QC continues later. Consent/transfer restrictions remain separate; records use synthetic aliases, lots, passages, actions and deviations.

cards.front: Bank lineage check: MCB vial M07 (passage 8, PDL 12.0) is expanded to WCB W03 with N0 = 1.0 × 10⁶ and Nf = 2.0 × 10⁶ viable cells. What parent and PDL belong on W03’s record?
cards.back: Parent = M07; child = W03; event = expansion, with timestamp, operator and supporting record. PDL increment = log₂(2.0/1.0) = 1, so W03 begins at cumulative PDL 13.0. A freezer move or tier relabel does not replace this derivation record.

cards.front: Ledger repair: previous PDL 9.0; N0 = 0.75 × 10⁶; Nf = 1.50 × 10⁶; displayed entry says “+2, PDL 11”. Recompute and state how to correct it.
cards.back: log₂(1.50/0.75) = log₂2 = 1, so cumulative PDL = 9.0 + 1 = 10.0. Retain the original and append an attributed, dated, reasoned correction linked to raw counts; one passage is not automatically one or two PDL.

cards.front: Mini-join: positive V1 → preparation P1 → batch F1 → medium lot B1; positive V2 → P2 → F2 → B1; negative V3 → P2 → F2 → B1. What is the bounded conclusion?
cards.back: Both positives share B1 through different prepared batches, so B1 is a common-exposure lead. V3 is an exposed negative comparison, so the join does not prove causation. Preserve V3 and enumerate other B1/F1/F2 exposures; do not collapse F1 and F2 into one preparation ID.

cards.front: Trace handoff: what turns “the same medium was probably used” into an auditable incident/deviation outline?
cards.back: Provide unique vessel → event/preparation → component-lot joins; parent and passage/PDL links; original timestamps, counts and observations; negative/unresolved records; containment and disposition; competing hypotheses; and an attributed handoff for local review. Apply ALCOA corrections. Deeper GLP/CLIA/CAPA belongs to planned layer-4 lab-quality-systems.
